decision: D-PR-23 Option E -- formalize the status quo. docs/private/PIPELINE_RELIABILITY_WAVE_PLAN.md sec 3 workstream (a) 'MATIF: arm or remove', and the D-PR-23 row of the decision table.
what_this_file_is: THE DECLARATION THAT AN ABSENCE IS DELIBERATE. There is no top-level configs/silver/dags/futures_eod_browser.json, no rendered input, no _DAG_SCHEDULES entry and no dag_schedules.auto.tfvars.json entry for the Euronext/MATIF browser leg -- and none of that is an oversight or an unfinished wiring task. The leg is BUILT and LINT-BOUND (producer, both transform halves, CONTRACT_MAP entries, task spec, storage paths, row floors, roll bindings, serving unit card) and it publishes ZERO rows because nothing fires it. Without this file that state reads as a gap: any future 'raw present, silver absent' detector, any descriptor-set audit, any reader counting futures_eod chains sees a leg that stalled. With it, the absence is a DECLARED state with a named gate and a named owner decision.
glob_note: Lives under dags/unarmed/ ON PURPOSE. scripts/silver/gen_sfn_inputs.load_descriptors globs configs/silver/dags/*.json NON-RECURSIVELY and lints every hit as a chain descriptor, so a marker sitting at the top level would either fail that lint or -- worse -- be rendered and armed. Same construction as dags/observability/pattern_records_daily.json. This file is NEVER rendered, NEVER validated as a descriptor, and NEVER arms anything.

arming_gate.name: Euronext SETTL. semantics
arming_gate.blocks: the ARM (Option A). Nothing else in this repo is waiting on it.
arming_gate.question: does the rendered live.euronext.com quote table's SETTL. column carry TODAY's settlement after the ~18:30 CET publish, or the PREVIOUS session's?
arming_gate.method: two live captures of EBM-DPAR on the SAME day -- one intraday, one post-19:00 CET -- diffed against the next morning's capture. Plan sec 10, open question 1.
arming_gate.why_it_blocks: CONTRACT_MAP pins settle_kind='settlement' for all three MATIF slugs on the strength of a probe that has never been run, while the plan record states the intraday SETTL. column carries the PREVIOUS settlement. The rendered table publishes NO DATE anywhere in its DOM (src/leviathan/storage/paths.py raw_euronext_key), so trade_date comes only from the raw key's as_of_date -- the fetch date. If SETTL. is T-1 at capture time the whole leg is silently off by one session and NO downstream check can detect it: not the row floors, not the census diff, not freshness, not the gate. Arming a leg with an undetectable off-by-one is the opposite of this wave's zero-repeat-offender standard.
arming_gate.on_resolution: probe S3 clearing does NOT arm anything by itself. It clears ONE of the arm preconditions below; the arm remains a separate, separately-approved decision.

leg.jobdef_note: EXISTS in AWS at revision 1 but is UNTRACKED BY TERRAFORM and carries NEITHER retryStrategy NOR attemptDurationSeconds (both null). Adopting it into terraform WITH those two is the other half of D-PR-23 and rides the POST-FREEZE TERRAFORM BATCH (plan sec 5.2). This file does not arm it, register it, or modify it.
leg.silver_rows_note: ZERO. The 22 leviathan_slug= prefixes under silver/futures_eod/ contain no MATIF slug.

orphan_raw_objects.disposition: RETAIN. Do not delete, do not run through build_bronze, do not treat as a stalled leg.
orphan_raw_objects.what_they_are: the W1c one-shot proof capture -- one rendered table.html per product (EBM-DPAR / EMA-DPAR / ECO-DPAR). They are the ONLY objects under the source=euronext prefix, and they are the measurement the EURONEXT row floors were counted from (tests/fixtures/w1c/capture_notes.md).
orphan_raw_objects.why_retain: they are evidence, not backlog. Deleting them would destroy the provenance of the row floors; promoting them to silver would land three MATIF slugs' worth of rows dated by a fetch date whose settlement semantics probe S3 has not yet resolved -- exactly the off-by-one this declaration exists to prevent.
orphan_raw_objects.detector_note: a future 'raw present, silver absent' detector MUST read this declaration before flagging the source=euronext prefix. Raw-without-silver here is the declared state, not a stall.

serving_disposition.summary: every MATIF lookup DECLINES honestly, and it declines rather than errors.
serving_disposition.mechanism: PRICE_COVERAGE_START (src/leviathan/silver/futures_eod_contracts.py) has NO entry for any MATIF slug -- ABSENT slug == NOT SERVED. coverage_start_for() raises ValueError rather than defaulting; leviathan.graphrag.numbers.agent.futures_eod_route catches that ValueError and returns ('uncovered', None); the executor sees a route in FUTURES_EOD_COVERAGE_CLASSES and returns status='declined' with the verbatim scope_note BEFORE ANY SQL COMPILES. The raise never reaches a caller.
serving_disposition.separability: this is why arm and flip are two independently gateable decisions. MATIF rows can land in silver_futures_eod and every MATIF answer stays BYTE-IDENTICAL until PRICE_COVERAGE_START gains an entry. silver_futures_eod is also not in cascade_map.yaml, so landing rows cannot perturb the gate's vocabulary checks either.
serving_disposition.flip_is_a_separate_decision: adding a PRICE_COVERAGE_START entry is D-PR-24, DEFERRED and gated after R6. It is NOT unlocked by probe S3 and NOT unlocked by arming the ingest. Two eval rows and four unit-test assertions encode the decline as current truth.

freshness_blindspot.statement: family-level freshness CANNOT see a MATIF-only stall, under this declaration or under a future arm.
freshness_blindspot.why: silver_freshness_slas['futures_eod'] is the ONLY SLA for the family and freshness reads the newest canonical object across the whole family. Four healthy legs keep the clock fresh regardless of what MATIF does.
freshness_blindspot.under_a_future_arm: rows would land that NOTHING READS (the flip is separate), so a leg that stops writing is invisible to every consumer-side check; the per-source row floor and the gate census would be the only detectors.
freshness_blindspot.owner: per-leg freshness granularity is D-EI-12 / R7's. Reference it; do not fork it here.

row_floors_if_armed.source_of_truth: EURONEXT_MIN_ROWS in src/leviathan/transforms/raw_to_bronze/euronext_eod.py and _MIN_SILVER_ROWS_PER_DAY_EURONEXT in jobs/batch/futures_eod_task.py. The numbers above are a MIRROR for readability and are pinned to those two by test.
row_floors_if_armed.hazard: three independent hard-fail surfaces per fire, all alarming. A legitimate venue delisting of a single expiry (which the code correctly treats as a code change) REDS the leg until a human re-counts and re-pins -- a plausible repeat-offender shape. Its runbook must be decided BEFORE the arm, not discovered after.

arm_preconditions.note: ALL of these are non-negotiable and NONE of them is discharged by this file. Listed so a future arm is a checklist rather than a rediscovery. Plan sec 3 workstream (a), Option A.
items: probe S3 run and settle_kind corrected or confirmed (see arming_gate above)
a route-discovery probe for any Euronext downloadable price history endpoint; the repo documents none, but that is an absence-of-evidence read, not a measured negative

SEED s3://leviathan-dev-shahem-001/cascade_census/rolling/futures_eod_browser/census.json via jobs/audit/advance_rolling_census.py BEFORE the first fire. silver_rebuild_gate raises BaselineFetchError and FAILS CLOSED on an absent baseline, so an unseeded new schedule REDS on its very first fire -- a guaranteed self-inflicted alert. Do NOT point it at the SUPERSEDED family-level rolling/futures_eod/census.json that futures_eod_free.json's own gate_baseline_uri_note forbids.

its OWN descriptor and its OWN cron. Folding it into futures_eod_free would violate this leg's cadence contract for ~7 months of the year: the contract is stated in CET-local terms (fire AFTER the ~18:30 CET publish and BEFORE local midnight) while the default as_of_date is UTC-today, and a 22:30Z fire is 00:30 CEST in summer. That is a design decision, not a wiring task.
scripts/silver/futures_eod_gate.py _DAG_SCHEDULES gains the third entry, or gate 8 never emits this chain's silver_rebuild_gate command at all
leviathan-dev-browser-runner adopted into terraform WITH retryStrategy and attemptDurationSeconds (post-freeze batch, plan sec 5.2)
the dag_schedules.auto.tfvars.json entry -- which is what actually arms the fire -- authored and reviewed in the batch, never hand-fired

rejected_alternatives.remove_from_price_vocabulary: NOT POSSIBLE as the code stands. config_check asserts CONTRACT_MAP covers EXACTLY the configs/commodities/*.yaml stems; taking it would mean relaxing that equality to a subset rule and retiring the '31 auditable rather than aspirational' invariant.
rejected_alternatives.full_removal: REJECTED with citation. 72 tracked files, three causal DAGs, four Athena DDLs, feature/training configs; zero precedent (git log --diff-filter=D over configs/commodities/*.yaml returns no deletions in repo history); and it would delete a contract the REASONING lane actively serves -- four eval rows use french_wheat_matif and test_cascade.py pins its primary title.

rollback: none owed. This declaration changes no runtime behaviour: it adds no schedule, no descriptor, no coverage entry, no alarm and no AWS resource.
